title: Rifles Across the Desert: The Spring That Ended Songhay
summary: Recounts how, in fifteen ninety-one, the four-thousand-strong musket army that the Moroccan Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur sent beyond the Sahara — misinformed about where the gold mines actually lay — marched for months across the desert and then, on the thirteenth of March at Tondibi, scattered a Songhay army many times its size. The episode stretches from the sacking of Gao and Timbuktu to the scholar Ahmad Baba being carried off in chains to Marrakesh, and to the gold they sought never being found at all.
